1 12 12 NA NA No Three new courses are associated with this certificate and are under review in Kuali.
One course is truly new.
EDC 664: Equity & Justice in College Teaching This course is designed to introduce students to collegiate-level equity pedagogies.
The course begins with a brief overview of various theoretical perspectives on equity and justice in higher education teaching.
Then, the course surveys equity- oriented strategies for course design and delivery.
Students will have the opportunity to critically reflect on various approaches and tools that they might utilize in their future careers.
Two new courses have been successfully offered in the past as special topics courses.
EDC 511: Critical Dialogues on Race in Postsecondary Education Many people talk about race-based inequities in education and society; few have explored structured techniques for the most productive critical dialogues.
This course will explore contemporary challenges and solutions to teaching and training adults around issues of race and racism in the United States.

The Graduate Certificate in Community Planning (CP) is an online program that helps students develop core competencies in sustainable Community Planning.
Through this program, students will gain a foundation in the principles and practices of community planning and development, specifically in areas of land use and environmental planning.
The history of planning has many examples of environmental injustice, in which land use decisions have privileged some communities over others.
A commitment to anti-racism, inclusiveness, equity, as well as spatial and social justice perspectives is an integral part of a planning education.
Students can earn their certificate in four sessions, maximizing flexibility and convenience for career enhancement, leadership positions in the industry, and professional growth.
The Community Planning online certificate aligns with the University's commitment to urban initiative, community engagement and solving the world's most important challenges by equiping students with practical knowledge and understanding of how to plan for and enable equitable and sustainable communities.

This 4-course asychonous online graduate certificate also creates a learning opportunity for students who may not be able to attend graduate school in person on a full time basis, thereby creating a diverse learning opportunity (goal 3 of the URI Stragic Priority 2) and increase graduate student enrollment (goal 2 of Strategic Priority 2).
The impact of a working public better informed in values and strategies of community planning should contribute to healthier and more sustainable communities environmentally, socially and economically.
The online graduate Community Planning certificate will open doors for recent college graduates as well as working professionals; they will become eligible for positions and promotion in a growing job market.
By combining this online certificate with other stackable certificates such as Public Administration, MEM and GIS, students will be well equipped to engage in the significant planning challenges of our time.
Our department currently offers an in-person Graduate Certificate in Community Planning.
This proposed new program will be offered in the 7-week online format and require 4 classes with 3 required classes and one elective (12 credits).

Our existing Community Planning Graduate Certificate requires 5 courses to complete the certificate (15 or 16 credits).
The asychonous online certitificate is intended for a different student population from our in-person gradute certificate and provides somewhat different content.
The online certificate content is pragmatically planned to be useful for working professionals, adapted for online delivery, and geared towards working professionals who do not have prior knowledge of planning.
The purpose of the Certificate is to give these students a way to quickly and remotely attain a basic knowledge of planning, and to stack that knowledge with other certificates, such as Public Policy, Marine Affairs, GIS, etc.
By contrast, the full semester, in-person planning program encompasses a wide and in-depth disciplinary space, with opportunities to learn from in-person university relationships and pursue independent research, while still providing future planners with knowledge and tools for professional work.

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE 224 PASTORE HALL, 51 LOWER COLLEGE ROAD, KINGSTON, RI 02881 USA, P: 401.874.2616 Faculty Senate Resolution 2024-2025-03 Faculty Senate Meeting of January 23, 2025 Resolution on the Implementation of Honors Contracts WHEREAS, following considerable self-study and significant input from external experts, the URI Honors Program has proposed the use of honors contracts at URI.
Honors contracts are formal agreements, facilitated by an honors program, between a student and instructor.
They allow students and instructors to enhance non-honors courses to an honors level through additional learner-directed work tailored to the “broader, deeper, and more complex” learning experiences advocated by the National Collegiate Honors Council (NCHC); and WHEREAS, contracts are recognized by over 60% of honors programs in the USA, where they foster community and ownership by enhancing the educational process and commitment to the programs’ success.
For example, work at the University Honors Program at the University of Kansas shows that honors contracts act as far more than stopgaps to address honors course shortages.

They can “facilitate access to honors, increases completion, democratize key aspects of the honors experience, provide students with structured avenues for building relationships with faculty members, and empower students to own their educational experiences”; and WHEREAS, honors contracts may be best understood as a form of an independent study, entered into voluntarily by both students and faculty, with a contract defining outcomes, deadlines, and assessment definitions for additional work related to the course materials; and WHEREAS, honors contracts provide flexibility for students to align their education with their interests and goals.
They also allow programs to meet student needs when student/faculty constraints or funding limitations preclude offering stand-alone honors courses that fit student interests and needs; and WHEREAS, Contracts provide an extra measure of curricular flexibility at institutions such as ours that are not able to field enough faculty, cannot provide an adequate number of honors courses, or do not have a large enough student body to fill honors sections.

Contracts can fill the gap and provide opportunities for the self-guided intellectual growth of students; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Faculty Senate of the University of Rhode Island calls for implementation of the following Honors Contracts Proposal.
This includes making the

recommended changes to the University Catalog and to the eCampus system used by Enrollment Services; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Honors Program is called upon to reflect these changes on their website and in all other promotional and outreach materials promulgated by the Program. The Program is also called upon to review Chapter 8 of the University Manual (Academic Regulations, Honors Program) in light of the Contracts Proposal and bring any recommended changes to the Faculty Senate expeditiously; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the authority to offer Honors Contracts enabled by this resolution shall not extend beyond the Fall 2025 semester; and BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that no instructor may participate in more than three Honors Contracts in a single semester. Adopted this 23rd day of January, 2025. ____________________________________________________________ T heodore Walls, URI Faculty Senate President

FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION April 16, 2026 Graduate Council Report 2025-2026-6B At the April 6, 2026 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate PROGRAM MODIFICATIONS COLLEGE OF BUSINESS Professional Science Masters - PSM, Effective Spring 2027 The Professional Science Masters (PSM) program is a non-thesis graduate degree program that prepares students for leadership and management roles in science- and technology-driven organizations.
Housed in the College of Business, the PSM integrates advanced scientific or technical coursework with professional skills in leadership, project management, communication, and applied problem solving that are broadly applicable in rapidly evolving scientific fields.
This 30–33 credit interdisciplinary degree combines a graduate certificate in a science or technical field with professional business coursework and applied experiential learning.

Students develop practical interpersonal, leadership, communication, and critical thinking skills, and apply these competencies in real-world organizational and industry contexts.
The PSM requires the completion of a graduate certificate in a science field, and four professional courses, including at least one capstone/practicum, and an additional relevant graduate-level course(s) from the URI Online portfolio as elective with Program Director approval.
PSM program tracks that have been certified by the National Professional Science Master's Association should have Industry Advisory Boards and include an integrative, hands-on experiential learning project or applied internship.
The menu of professional courses includes BUS532, BUS506, BUS509, BUS515, MBA540, and BUS557 (MBA557).
Other online courses may be approved by the program director.
At least one 3-credit course must be a capstone/practicum.

If a student does not take BUS515 and the certificate program does not contain a capstone experience, they should take another capstone course from the URI Online portfolio (e.g., PSC592 or MPS598) In addition to the graduate certificate courses, the four professional courses, and the capstone/practicum, students must complete relevant graduate-level course(s) from the URI Online portfolio as electives with Program Director approval (up to 6 credits).

Textiles, Fashion Merchandising and Design - ABM, Effective Fall 2026 Textiles, Fashion Merchandising and Design (TMD) Department offers an Accelerated Bachelor of Science to Master of Science Degree in Textiles, Fashion Merchandising and Design (ABMTMD) to allow undergraduates to complete a BS/BA and an MS degree in 5 years.
The program would allow students currently receiving a Bachelor’s of Science in Textiles, Fashion Merchandising and Design; or a Bachelor’s of Science in Textile Marketing; or Bachelor’s degree in any other major combined with a TMD minor Under certain circumstances, students enrolled in programs leading to degrees in related areas may be considered for admission into the TMD program, for example, Business, Chemistry, History, Art History, or Psychology.
In such cases, half of the total credits must be in TMD.
As part of the program, ABMTMD students will need to earn a total of 33 credits (including 11 credits double-counted from their undergraduate degree) Students will also complete industry-oriented capstone project as an independent study (for example, complete an industry-focused case study or an industry-sponsored project).

Finally, students will also successfully complete comprehensive exams on two TMD elective courses.
Courses eligible for double-counting: TMD403 Textile Performance TMD413 Dyeing and Finishing Textiles TMD424 Retail Product Trend Forecasting TMD426 Historic and Contemporary Furniture TMD432 Fashion Retail Supply Chain Management TMD433 Textile Markets TMD434 Branding Fashion Industry TMD440 Historic Textiles TMD441 History of Western Dress TMD442 Fashion Promotion TMD458 Fashion Retail Analytics URI courses outside the TMD Department that are cataloged as eligible for graduate credits can double-count.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCE Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling - MS, Effective Summer 2026 The Master's in Mental and Behavioral Health Counseling program prepares graduates to work with clients in settings including counseling agencies, hospitals, community mental health centers, and private practice.
Students gain training in evidence-based practice, measurement-based care, develop practical skills in individual and group therapy approaches, as well as career counseling with diverse populations.

This 66-credit program meets curricular requirements for the State of Rhode Island's Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC).
Course Requirements: HDF450, HDF551, HDF570, PSY507, PSY603, PSY615 (3 credits), PSY642, PSY643, PSY644, PSY660, PSY666, PSY670 (18 credits), and PSY672 (12 credits).
A minimum of 66 credits is required to graduate.
